build.method: git archive HEAD into an OS temp directory, then go build -o <temp>/fak4213.exe ./cmd/fak

probes.name: guarded_codex_split_auto
probes.interpretation: On this non-multiplexer PowerShell host, split=auto did not cause a start-time exit; it behaved equivalently to split=off. This rules out the auto-selection path here, not an actually-created multiplexer info pane.

probes.name: launch_loop_gate
probes.interpretation: The launch gate refuses synchronously before spawning Codex and prints an explicit reason. It does not explain a child rollout that starts and then truncates mid-turn.

probes.name: nonzero_child_exit_control
probes.command: <temp>/fak4213.exe guard ... -- codex exec <intentionally malformed argv control>
probes.interpretation: The new durable witness distinguishes an ordinary nonzero child teardown from clean completion.

probes.name: controlled_mid_turn_runtime_force_kill
probes.command: Start committed-tip fak guard with a correctly quoted long-running codex exec; enumerate descendants; Stop-Process -Force the native codex.exe runtime after thread start

journal_terminal_row.reason: NONZERO_EXIT on the witnessed build; follow-up fixes Windows 0xFFFFFFFF forced termination to SIGNAL_CRASH/-1

probes.interpretation: A force-killed native Codex runtime propagates through node/cmd to the guard and now leaves a durable terminal row. The observed Windows forced-termination spelling exposed a classifier bug (0xFFFFFFFF treated as ordinary nonzero), fixed in the follow-up code change.

privacy: Prompts are fixed synthetic sentinels and omitted. Session UUIDs, absolute paths, stdout text, and credentials are not retained.
verdict: CONTROLLED KILL PROVEN: force-killing the native codex.exe runtime mid-turn propagates as guarded-child abnormal termination and leaves a durable CHILD_CRASH witness. Split auto/off both complete normally on this host, and the launch loop-gate refuses before child launch. The exact historical spontaneous killer remains NOT_REPRODUCED; future Windows force kills are normalized from 0xFFFFFFFF to SIGNAL_CRASH/-1.
